chunks: You have stated that I killed Ṭalḥah and az-Zubayr, forced ‘Ā’ishah out of her house and adopted residence between the two cities (Kūfah and Baṣrah). These are matters with which you have no concern nor do they involve anything against you. Therefore, no explanation about them is due to you.

key_terms.بَيْنَ الْمِصْرَيْنِ: between the two cities, referring to Kufah and Basra
key_terms.بِعَائِشَةَ: with Aisha bint Abi Bakr, the wife of the Prophet
key_terms.طَلْحَةَ: Talhah ibn Ubaydullah, a prominent companion
key_terms.وَالزُّبَيْرَ: and az-Zubayr ibn al-Awwam, a prominent companion

ai.seo_question: What is Imam Ali's response to Muawiya regarding the Battle of the Camel?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) counters Muawiya’s accusations by highlighting the latter's absence from the Battle of the Camel, thereby nullifying his claim to authority or accountability. This response underscores the Shia scholarly view that Muawiya’s critique was politically motivated rather than based on direct witness, emphasizing that the Caliph’s actions were divinely guided and not subject to the judgment of those who were merely observers.
